title: Large Language Model Hacking: Quantifying the Hidden Risks of Using LLMs for Text Annotation

bias_targets.methodology: The paper evaluates 13 million LLM annotations across 37 diverse computational social science tasks to quantify how implementation choices (e.g., model selection, prompt phrasing) introduce systematic measurement errors. It measures the risk of these biases propagating to downstream statistical hypothesis tests and causing Type I (false positive), Type II (false negative), Type S (wrong sign), and Type M (exaggerated magnitude) errors.

The authors analyze the variance in statistical outcomes resulting from 'researcher degrees of freedom' by systematically altering LLM configurations (using 18 different models and 199 prompt paraphrases) to measure the feasibility of intentionally or accidentally manufacturing statistically significant scientific conclusions from both null and true effects.
